rules.name: SQL query built from a template literal with interpolation
rules.message: Untrusted data appears to be interpolated directly into a SQL string passed to query()/execute(). Use a parameterized query instead.

rules.name: SQL query built via string concatenation
rules.message: SQL string is concatenated with a variable before being executed. Use a parameterized query instead of string concatenation.

rules.name: SQL query built from an f-string
rules.message: An f-string is passed directly to execute(). Use a parameterized query with placeholders instead.

rules.name: SQL query built via string concatenation
rules.message: SQL string is concatenated with a variable before being executed. Use a parameterized query instead.

rules.name: SQL query built via %-formatting
rules.message: SQL string uses %-formatting instead of a parameterized query placeholder passed as a separate argument.

rules.name: SQL query built via string concatenation
rules.message: Use PreparedStatement with bind parameters instead of concatenating a SQL string.

rules.name: SQL query built via string concatenation
rules.message: Use a prepared statement with bind_param() instead of concatenating user input into the query string.

rules.name: SQL query built via string concatenation
rules.message: Use a parameterized query ($1, $2, ... or ?) instead of concatenating the SQL string.

rules.name: Shell command built from a template literal with interpolation
rules.message: Untrusted data is interpolated into a shell command. Use execFile/execFileSync with an argument array instead of exec/execSync.

rules.name: Shell command built via string concatenation
rules.message: Use execFile/execFileSync with an argument array instead of building a shell command string.

rules.name: Use of eval()
rules.message: eval() executes its argument as code. If any part of the argument can be influenced by user input, this is arbitrary code execution.

rules.name: Use of the Function constructor
rules.message: new Function(...) compiles and executes a string as code, equivalent in risk to eval() if input is untrusted.

rules.name: Shell command built via f-string or concatenation
rules.message: Pass a list of arguments to subprocess.run() with shell=False instead of building a shell command string.

rules.name: subprocess call with shell=True
rules.message: shell=True invokes a shell to interpret the command string. Prefer shell=False with an argument list, especially if any part of the command is derived from input.

rules.name: Use of eval()/exec()
rules.message: eval()/exec() execute their argument as code. If any part can be influenced by user input, this is arbitrary code execution.

rules.name: Shell command built via string concatenation
rules.message: Untrusted data is concatenated into a shell command. Use escapeshellarg() on every interpolated value, or avoid shelling out.

rules.name: Use of eval()
rules.message: eval() executes its argument as PHP code. If any part of the argument can be influenced by user input, this is arbitrary code execution.

rules.name: Shell command built via string concatenation
rules.message: Use the ProcessBuilder overload that takes an argument array instead of a concatenated command string.

rules.name: Shell command built via string concatenation
rules.message: Pass the binary and its arguments directly to exec.Command instead of building a shell -c string.

rules.name: Hardcoded credential or key
rules.message: A credential-looking literal is assigned directly in source. Load it from an environment variable or secret manager instead.

rules.name: AWS access key ID in source
rules.message: This matches the format of an AWS access key ID. Rotate the key and load credentials from environment/secret manager instead.

rules.name: Private key embedded in source
rules.message: A PEM private key block is committed directly in source. Move it to a secrets store and rotate the key.

rules.name: Stripe live secret key in source
rules.message: This matches the format of a live Stripe secret key. Rotate it and load it from environment/secret manager instead.

rules.name: Slack token in source
rules.message: This matches the format of a Slack API token. Rotate it and load it from environment/secret manager instead.

rules.name: GitHub token in source
rules.message: This matches the format of a GitHub personal access / OAuth token. Rotate it and load it from environment/secret manager instead.

rules.name: Assignment to innerHTML
rules.message: Assigning to innerHTML with unsanitized input allows script injection. Use textContent, or sanitize with a library like DOMPurify if HTML is required.

rules.name: Use of dangerouslySetInnerHTML
rules.message: React's XSS protection is bypassed here. Ensure the HTML is sanitized (e.g., with DOMPurify) before rendering.

rules.name: Use of document.write()
rules.message: document.write() with unsanitized input can inject script content into the page.

rules.name: Use of Vue v-html directive
rules.message: v-html renders raw HTML without escaping. Ensure the bound value is sanitized before use.

rules.name: Jinja2 |safe filter disables autoescaping
rules.message: The |safe filter disables Jinja2's autoescaping for this value. Confirm the value cannot contain user-controlled HTML.

rules.name: Django mark_safe() disables escaping
rules.message: mark_safe() tells Django not to escape this value. Confirm it cannot contain user-controlled HTML.

rules.name: Template built from an f-string
rules.message: Building the template itself from an f-string with user input can allow template/HTML injection. Pass user data as render variables instead.

rules.name: Echoing a superglobal directly
rules.message: User input is echoed without escaping. Use htmlspecialchars() before output.

rules.name: File path built from request input
rules.message: A request-controlled value is joined into a file path. Normalize and verify the resolved path stays within the intended base directory.

rules.name: File read using request-controlled path
rules.message: A file is read using a path derived from request input without an apparent containment check.

rules.name: File opened using request-controlled path
rules.message: A file is opened using a path derived from request input without an apparent containment check.

rules.name: File path built from request parameter
rules.message: A File is constructed from a request parameter without an apparent containment check against a base directory.

rules.name: File operation using a superglobal directly
rules.message: A file is opened/included using unvalidated request input. This can also lead to remote code execution via include/require.

rules.name: File opened using request-controlled path
rules.message: A file is opened using a path derived from request input without an apparent containment check.

rules.name: Use of MD5/SHA-1
rules.message: MD5 and SHA-1 are not suitable for password hashing or security-sensitive integrity checks. Use bcrypt/scrypt/Argon2 for passwords, SHA-256+ for integrity.

rules.name: Use of MD5/SHA-1
rules.message: MD5 and SHA-1 are not suitable for password hashing or security-sensitive integrity checks. Use bcrypt/scrypt/Argon2 for passwords, SHA-256+ for integrity.

rules.name: Use of MD5/SHA-1
rules.message: MD5 and SHA-1 are not suitable for password hashing or security-sensitive integrity checks. Use bcrypt/scrypt/Argon2 for passwords, SHA-256+ for integrity.

rules.name: Use of AES in ECB mode
rules.message: ECB mode does not hide data patterns and is considered insecure. Use an authenticated mode such as GCM.

rules.name: Math.random() (low confidence — review context)
rules.message: Math.random() is not cryptographically secure. Flag for review only if used to generate tokens, session IDs, or password-reset codes; use crypto.randomBytes()/randomUUID() for those.

rules.name: Use of md5()/sha1()
rules.message: MD5 and SHA-1 are not suitable for password hashing. Use password_hash() with PASSWORD_BCRYPT/PASSWORD_ARGON2ID.

rules.name: Deep merge of request body into an object
rules.message: Deep-merging request-controlled JSON into an object can allow __proto__/constructor.prototype pollution. Validate/allowlist keys or use a merge utility with prototype-pollution protection.

rules.name: Bracket access to __proto__
rules.message: Bracket-notation access to __proto__ (read or write), especially where the key can come from request data, is a prototype pollution primitive.

rules.name: Direct __proto__ assignment
rules.message: Direct assignment to an object's __proto__ property can pollute the prototype chain for all instances.

rules.name: Outbound request to a request-controlled URL
rules.message: The destination URL comes directly from request input. Validate scheme/host and block internal/link-local ranges before fetching.

rules.name: Outbound request to a request-controlled URL
rules.message: The destination URL comes directly from request input. Validate scheme/host and block internal/link-local ranges before fetching.

rules.name: Outbound request to a request-controlled URL
rules.message: The destination URL comes directly from request input. Validate scheme/host and block internal/link-local ranges before fetching.

rules.name: cURL target URL from a superglobal
rules.message: The cURL destination URL comes directly from request input. Validate scheme/host and block internal/link-local ranges before fetching.

rules.name: file_get_contents() on a superglobal
rules.message: If this URL points at a remote resource, the destination comes directly from request input. Validate scheme/host before fetching.

rules.name: Outbound request to a request-controlled URL
rules.message: The destination URL comes directly from request input. Validate scheme/host and block internal/link-local ranges before fetching.
